newsitem.title: SPAIN: HUGHES' DIRECTV IN TALKS TO TAKE VIA DIGITAL STAKE.
newsitem.headline: HUGHES' DIRECTV IN TALKS TO TAKE VIA DIGITAL STAKE.

text.p: Spain's Via Digital said on Friday it was in talks with DirecTV, the satellite television division of giant Hughes Electronics, regarding the purchase of a significant stake in the Spanish digital television platform.
"Via Digital is currently in talks with the Hughes/Galaxy/DirecTV group over the incorporation of the said group with a significant stake in its shareholding," Via Digital said in a statement.
Via Digital is Spain's second digital television platform which plans to begin commercial operations in September.

The Via Digital project, in conjunction with Telefonica, RTVE, Televisa, independent television stations and Spanish newspapers and magazines, will offer 35 channels including film, sport and specialised information.

DirecTV is the United States' largest satellite TV service with 52 percent of the digital television market and offering 37 channels in its most basic package. It has access to three satellites in orbit.
Galaxy Latin America was formed in 1995 by Hughes, Cisneros, Mexico's MVS Multivision and Brasil's Televisao to offer DirecTV in Latin America.
